messages.content: 你能使用 get_stock_prices 函數來檢索蘋果、微軟、亞馬遜和特斯拉分別在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內的股價嗎？。

function.name: get_stock_prices
function.description: Retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

companies.description: List of companies to retrieve stock prices for.

duration.description: Time duration to retrieve stock prices for. E.g., '1 week', '2 weeks', '1 month', etc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to use get_stock_prices function to fetch Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN) and Tesla (TSLA). They want separate durations: "1 week", "2 weeks", "3 weeks" and "1 month". The request says "for each company respectively"? It might mean we need to call with multiple companies? But they say "in 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks and 1 month time ranges." Possibly means we should provide data for all four companies across those periods.

We can either make one call per period or combine into single calls. The function signature expects an array of companies and a duration. So we could do four calls:

Call 1: companies ["Apple","Microsoft"], duration "1 week"
But maybe better to include all four companies each time? That would give same set repeated but different durations. Or we could group them differently: e.g., first two companies for 1 week, next two for 2 weeks... unclear.

User said "蘋果、微軟、亞馬遜和特斯拉分別在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內的股價". Means "the stock price of Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Tesla respectively within 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks and 1 month time range." This implies mapping: Apple -> 1 week; Microsoft -> 2 weeks; Amazon -> 3 weeks; Tesla -> 1 month. Yes likely that's what they intend: each company has its own duration.

Thus we will call get_stock_prices separately for each pair: For Apple with duration "1 week"; Microsoft with "2 weeks"; Amazon with "3 weeks"; Tesla with "1 month".

Return results accordingly. We'll produce JSON output summarizing each company's data. Use function calls sequentially. Let's proceed.
